wu: Play 'Simon Says' with body parts and health actions (e.g., 'Simon says touch your head', 'Simon says pretend to cough'). Students stand up and follow commands. Teacher models and corrects pronunciation.
wuAlt: Play 'Charades' with body parts and illness actions (e.g., 'sneeze', 'stomach ache') for students to guess.
Use flashcards of body parts/illnesses for a quick 'What's missing?' game.
pres: Show flashcards of common illnesses (headache, cold, stomach ache) and model advice: 'You should drink water' or 'You shouldn't eat ice cream'. Use a doctor-patient dialogue with a puppet to demonstrate. Check understanding with 'What should I do if I have a headache?'
presAlt: Read a simple health leaflet from 'res' and highlight 'should/shouldn't' sentences.
Use a story about a character with a cold and elicit advice from students.
prac: Play 'Doctor Says' in pairs: one student pretends to have an illness, the other gives advice using 'should/shouldn't'. Teacher circulates to correct and model. Use sentence frames on the board for support.
pracAlt: Complete a gap-fill worksheet with 'should/shouldn't' and health vocabulary.
Play 'Advice Race': teams write correct advice for illnesses on the board.
ls: Listen to a doctor-patient dialogue from 'res' and circle the correct advice (e.g., 'should rest' or 'should play football'). Check answers as a class.
re: Play 'Pass the Action': students pass a ball and say a health advice sentence (e.g., 'You should sleep') while doing an action (yawn, stretch).
prod: Roleplay 'Advice Column' in pairs: one student writes a problem (e.g., 'I have a stomach ache'), the other gives advice. Swap roles. Teacher monitors for correct language use.
rw: Read a 'Problem Page' from 'res' and write advice for 3 problems using 'should/shouldn't'. Share answers with a partner.
st: Sing the 'Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes' song with actions. Close with: 'Today you gave health advice with should/shouldn't. Thank you, class!'
g: Students follow commands with 'should/shouldn't' (e.g., 'You shouldn't run').
Act out illnesses for others to guess and give advice.
Teams write advice for illnesses on the board.
Pass a ball and say advice with an action.
Read and write advice for health problems.
diff: Fast finishers: write a dialogue for a doctor-patient scenario.
Support: use sentence frames with 'should/shouldn't' and vocabulary lists.
hw: Write advice for 3 health problems (e.g., 'My friend has a cold').
Draw a comic strip showing someone giving advice.
Record a voice message giving advice for an illness.
tip: Use real-life examples from students' experiences (e.g., 'What should you do if you eat too much couscous?') to make the language relevant.
